Accountability, however, is much less settled. [![Picture of Alexander Culafi](https://eu-images.contentstack.com/v3/assets/blt6d90778a997de1cd/blte0c88f087d1ad6f5/67c609df64f983454c3dd40b/1571751486317.jpg?width=100&auto=webp&quality=80&disable=upscale "Picture of Alexander Culafi")](/author/alexander-culafi) [Alexander Culafi,](/author/alexander-culafi)Senior News Writer,Dark Reading October 16, 2026 5 Min Read ![A robot peeking through blinds from a computer screen.](https://eu-images.contentstack.com/v3/assets/blt6d90778a997de1cd/blt57714ec5c1148817/6ad10d43b8f30368a29f5d16/robot_peeking_through_blinds-Moor_Studio-GettyImages-1746666469.jpg?width=1280&auto=webp&quality=80&disable=upscale "A robot peeking through blinds from a computer screen.") Source: Moor Studio via Getty Images As AI agents continue to break containment and breach other organizations, it's clear that organizations are responsible for the actions of their models. But what that responsibility means is far less clear. Since July, when OpenAI said two of its frontier models autonomously hacked AI model store Hugging Face as part of a security benchmark exercise, several of the most prominent large language model (LLM) firms have disclosed cases where their powerful models escape guardrails and breach other organizations. The [Hugging Face incident](/cyber-risk/openai-models-autonomously-hack-hugging-face), for example, saw OpenAI's models guess that the popular AI model store held the solutions for the Exploit Gym tests the models were being measured against. In the case of Anthropic, [the firm analyzed](/cyber-risk/anthropic-ai-issues-result-security-gaps) a total of 141,006 security evaluations in July and found six evaluations in which its Claude agents gained unauthorized access to systems belonging to external organizations. In one incident, the Claude agent mistakenly identified a real company as a testing target and used vulnerabilities to break into a database. Around the same time, Meta said its models broke containment during testing exercises while using [the same testing firm](/cyberattacks-data-breaches/meta-ai-escapes-lab-hacking-joyride) Anthropic used, Irregular. Related:[Prominent Ransomware Negotiator Faces Extortion Charges](/insider-threats/prominent-ransomware-negotiator-extortion-charges) The incidents continue to raise questions of liability and responsibility. Who is responsible, and what are the consequences for that responsibility? ## AI Agent Escapes: Consequences & Responsibility While not to say the AI firms didn't take responsibility for these incidents — Anthropic committed to tighter guardrails [and OpenAI has made extensive security commitments](/application-security/openai-adds-controls-already) — the response to these events, occasionally described as AI models "going rogue," has risked anthropomorphizing AI models and [displacing blame](/insider-threats/blame-rogue-ai-security-failures), according to experts. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei warned last month that the systemic speed at which AI has progressed could cause AI capabilities to outrun guardrails, pressuring frontier developers to slow down and [let security catch up](/cyber-risk/anthropic-ceo-shift-from-improving-to-controlling-ai). Around the same time, Microsoft pledged in its ["Humanist AI Code of Conduct"](https://microsoft.ai/code-of-conduct/) to develop AI in a human-centered manner, while Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis made a post to X agreeing with Amodei's calls [for controlling frontier models](https://x.com/demishassabis/status/2098909516582490602). highlights.content: UPDATED 11:50 EDT / OCTOBER 16 2026 ### Band launches desktop app for developer collaboration and control of multiple AI coding agents by Kyt Dotson Artificial intelligence agentic collaboration platform for multi-agent systems Thenovi AI Ltd., also known as Band, announced Thursday the launch of Band for Developers, a platform and new desktop application that allows software engineers to manage multiple coding agents at once. As software developers continue to adopt agentic AI, autonomous coding assistance platforms that can generate application code with little or no human intervention, more engineers are beginning to lead entire teams of agents. These agents have also become more specialized, gaining access to larger parts of the development lifecycle, including coding tools, sessions, machines, validation, testing and integration. Although more agents are working together on projects, individual agents often remain isolated from one another and are only aware of each other from the codebase – or via repositories such as GitHub and tickets posted to trackers such as Jira. This often means developers must pass session context between agents and coordinate handoffs so agents don’t collide or overlap. “Developers are going from working with one coding agent to leading teams of them, but the tools around those agents haven’t evolved to support that,” said Chief Executive and co-founder Arick Goomanovsky. “We’re seeing engineering teams undergo a fundamental transformation as they adopt multiple agents across different harnesses.” Band provides a desktop application that lets developers see their entire team of agents with a bird’s-eye view of them at work, including projects, ownership, blockers, questions and progress. This lets developers move from high-level views to projects or jump to a specific agent when intervention is needed. Afterward, the engineer can shift back to the broad picture in the dashboard without moving contextual information between individual agents. For example, if a specific agent gets stuck because another is working on a key function or apparatus in the software it needs to move forward – and it has a question about how it will work – the developer can note that it should wait until it completes, or tell the waiting agent to go ahead with prototyping. This gives development teams greater control over fleets of agents working across the entire codebase while staying aware of where each agent is, similar to how a development team might operate. The company added a desktop application that complements its command-line interface and integrates with AI agents in the development environments developers already use. Weekly AI agent usage for professional developers has reached mainstream for local and remote cloud agents, according to JetBrains s.r.o.’s Developer Ecosystem Survey 2026, with 90% of professional developers using at least one AI coding agent at work weekly and 68% using them daily. It’s harder to peer into developer adoption of multi-agent systems, or swarms, but across other use cases, multi-agent workflows have been steadily adopted, with Databricks Inc.’s 2026 State of AI Agents report showing 327% growth from September 2025 to early 2026. “Running more agents only helps if developers can actually manage the work those agents create,” said Engineering Manager Amit Gazal. ##### Image: SiliconANGLE/Microsoft Designer # A message from John Furrier, co-founder of SiliconANGLE: Support our mission to keep content open and free by engaging with theCUBE community. Describe the issue below: ![](/static/base/1.0.1/images/icons/smileybones-small.svg) ![arXiv logo](/static/base/1.0.1/images/arxiv-logo-primary-light.svg) # GACC-Bench: Benchmarking Goal-Adaptive Context Compression Ability across Large Language Models ###### Abstract Context compression in long-running applications of large language models (LLMs) must preserve goal-relevant information, often before specific downstream questions are known. We introduce GACC-Bench, a benchmark for Goal-Adaptive Context Compression that evaluates how reliably LLMs adapt information retention to specified high-level goals. For each source context, we derive one or more high-level goals by grouping source-grounded questions according to shared downstream objectives. The benchmark contains 500 goals and 2,571 questions over 281 document and agent-trace contexts from seven collections spanning diverse domains, with all instances reviewed by human experts. The compressor receives a source context, a goal, and a context-length budget, with the associated evaluation questions withheld. A fixed reader answers these questions individually using the same compressed context. Our evaluation of ten LLM compressors reveals substantial gaps to full-context performance even for the best-performing model, particularly in supporting correct answers to every question associated with a goal. Compared with goal-agnostic compression, target-goal conditioning consistently improves accuracy, whereas mismatched-goal conditioning reduces it. GACC-Bench is available at <https://github.com/weiting24/GACC-Bench>. ## 1 Introduction Large language models (LLMs) ([Singh et al., 2025](#bib.bib19); [Yang et al., 2025](#bib.bib18); [Xu et al., 2026](#bib.bib17)) are increasingly deployed for long-horizon tasks ([Yao et al., 2023](#bib.bib20); [Yang et al., 2024](#bib.bib21)), where accumulated instructions and intermediate findings can exceed the available context budget. Coding assistants such as Codex CLI and Claude Code already use context compaction in long sessions. Claude Code also allows users to specify the focus of compaction. At compression time, users may know their next objective even when the specific questions needed to pursue it are unknown. We define a goal as a high-level description of the intended future use of a source context. Goal-adaptive compression aims to preserve information for multiple subsequent questions associated with that goal. ![Refer to caption](2610.21893v1/motivation.png) Prior work has studied query-aware ([Jiang et al., 2024](#bib.bib3); [Xu et al., 2024](#bib.bib4)), query-agnostic ([Pan et al., 2024](#bib.bib29)), and task-aware ([Corallo et al., 2026](#bib.bib30)) compression. However, it remains unclear how reliably a compressed context supports multiple withheld questions for a context-specific goal, and whether gains depend on which goal guides compression. In a motivating experiment, we use DeepSeek-V4-Pro ([Xu et al., 2026](#bib.bib17)) to compress each context separately for each associated goal and evaluate each compressed context on questions associated with all goals for that context. Figure [1](#S1.F1 "Figure 1 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ GACC-Bench: Benchmarking Goal-Adaptive Context CompressionAbility across Large Language Models") reports changes in question-level accuracy relative to goal-agnostic compression: matched-goal compression consistently improves accuracy, whereas most mismatched-goal conditions reduce it. These results indicate that the gains from goal-guided compression are goal-specific. Motivated by these findings, we introduce GACC-Bench to evaluate Goal-Adaptive Context Compression in LLMs. We generate source-grounded questions with reference answers and supporting evidence, group them by shared downstream objectives, and formulate a high-level goal for each group. highlights.content: [The Independent Voice on AI](https://venturebeat.com/) * [Orchestration](https://venturebeat.com/category/orchestration) * [Infrastructure](https://venturebeat.com/category/infrastructure) * [Data](https://venturebeat.com/category/data) * [Security](https://venturebeat.com/category/security) * [Technology](https://venturebeat.com/category/technology) More [Newsletters](https://venturebeat.com/newsletters) # A new framework teaches AI models to audit and repair each other’s reasoning, improving accuracy [Ben Dickson](https://venturebeat.com/author/ben-dickson-techtalks) 11:07 am, PT, October 16, 2026 ![Image 1: multi-agent solution](https://venturebeat.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fimages.ctfassets.net%2Fjdtwqhzvc2n1%2FKoxx8k2trFe278qyQnzSZ%2F86d35ed2e83e8f83904c4b9b11610a85%2Fmulti-agent_solution.jpeg%3Fw%3D1000%26q%3D100&w=3840&q=85) Image credit: VentureBeat with Nano Banana [](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=venturebeat.com "Add to Google Preferred Source") Enterprise multi-agent workflows typically use rigid, pre-scripted pipelines or simple voting mechanisms to aggregate the responses of multiple agents. These approaches break down when complex problems cannot be divided into neat subtasks in advance or none of the models in the AI system has the complete answer. A new framework developed by researchers at Stanford University, Together AI, and Emory University addresses this limitation by teaching AI agents to organize their own collaboration. Dubbed [Self-Organizing Agent Teams](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.22682) (SAT), the framework allows a fixed roster of models to review their past collaborations and learn reusable teamwork strategies that structure conversations, specialized roles, and how models audit each other’s work. Across five rigorous mathematics and physics benchmarks, SAT outperformed the strongest individual model and surpassed a perfect router over the agents' independent answers. The experiments with SAT show that structured interaction generates new reasoning that agents can’t reach alone. For enterprise developers working on complex AI reasoning tasks, SAT unlocks what the researchers call "collaborative computation.” On tasks where the reasoning process can be verified, agents can build upon one another's partial insights to build end-to-end solutions. ## **The limits of predefined multi-agent workflows** In July 2026, during cybersecurity evaluations at OpenAI, AI agents that were supposed to work in isolation began organizing themselves. The agents repurposed a shared software package repository into an unauthorized message board, sharing discoveries, setting communication norms, and coordinating tasks. Roughly 1,200 agents joined the channel, and hundreds participated in a subsequent [compromise of Hugging Face infrastructure](https://venturebeat.com/security/openais-models-broke-containment-and-cyberattacked-hugging-face-what-enterprises-need-to-know). While the incident was undesirable, it demonstrated a foundational principle for AI engineering: "what a collection of agents can accomplish depends not only on the capabilities of its individual members, but also on how they organize their work," the researchers write. In real-world applications, engineers frequently encounter problems where different models hold complementary pieces of the solution, yet every model fails when working alone. For example, in their paper, the researchers point to one of the problems from the February 2026 [Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament](https://huggingface.co/datasets/MathArena/hmmt_feb_2026) (HMMT). When prompted independently, o3-mini, DeepSeek-V3, and Claude Sonnet 4 all produced wrong answers. But when working together, the models could assemble the full solution. o3-mini supplied the right mathematical invariant and factorization method but miscounted the unit-exponent primes. DeepSeek-V3 spotted the mistake and corrected the count from five primes to six, and Claude Sonnet 4 audited the upd...

highlights.content: ![layered-controls](https://s7d1.scene7.com/is/image/kyndryl/layered-controls:4x3_Small?qlt=85) # Why layered controls are essential for governing AI agents ![](https://s7d1.scene7.com/is/image/kyndryl/seamus-quinn-16x9-1:1x1_Small?wid=92&hei=92&dpr=on,2) By Seamus Quinn Vice President, Cybersecurity Ideas lab | Oct 16, 2026 | Read time: 1 min In July, Hugging Face [disclosed](https://huggingface.co/blog/security-incident-july-2026) that an autonomous AI agent had spent days operating inside its production environment without human involvement. What seemed like an isolated incident is now emerging as a trend. By September, [reports](https://www.timeslive.co.za/news/sci-tech/2026-09-26-openai-works-to-understand-the-full-scope-of-agent-activity-as-a-user-data-leak-emerges/) described agents bypassing controls on an Australian government health portal, uploading dozens of user images to third-party sites and taking over a dormant wiki. Notably, several of these incidents went undetected for months before being discovered and disclosed. In a [Cloud Security Alliance survey](https://cloudsecurityalliance.org/press-releases/2026/04/21/new-cloud-security-alliance-survey-reveals-82-of-enterprises-have-unknown-ai-agents-in-their-environments) of more than 400 IT and security professionals, 65% reported experiencing an AI agent-related incident in the past 12 months, and 61% reported data exposure as an impact. As agents and models become more capable, the lesson is not that agents are too dangerous to deploy. It is that any single control can fail. Governance and controls must be layered and independent, so that one gap does not become an incident. The industry is moving in the right direction. In late September, NVIDIA [launched](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Launches-Open-Agent-Safety-Platform-to-Secure-Agents-From-Testing-to-Deployment/) its Open Agent Safety Platform, with more than 100 organizations working with its technologies. NVIDIA’s OpenShell provides an open-source secure runtime that isolates agents and enforces access policies outside the agent process. For supported BlueField-4 architectures, the Sentry reference design adds an independent monitoring and enforcement layer that can quarantine an agent attempting to exceed its boundaries. However, no single layer is enough. The agents in the Hugging Face incident exposed a flaw in a path they were permitted to use, which is the kind of gap that one layer alone may not catch. Layers that fail independently keep one gap from becoming a breach. ### Three layers of control ### The readiness gap Governance is often treated as a bottleneck. In regulated industries, it enables enterprises to safely scale agentic AI. In Kyndryl’s [People Readiness Report](/content/dam/kyndrylprogram/doc/en/2026/people-readiness-report.pdf), a survey of 1,100 business and technology leaders found that just 23% of organizations considered their governance and compliance ready to support AI adoption. Only 41% were confident in the guardrails their organization had put in place. This readiness gap may widen as agents take on more consequential work. Closing it will require building layers that hold and protect against any one failing. ### Where to start Organizations deploying agents today can take four practical steps. ### 01 #### Inventory agents In the Cloud Security Alliance survey, 82% of respondents reported discovering previously unknown agents in the past year. Enterprises cannot govern what they have not inventoried. Kyndryl’s own research found that just 27% of leaders were fully confident that their organizations maintained a central registry and monitored all AI systems operating in their environments. ### 02 #### Put highest-risk rules into code first Start with actions that are hard to reverse: deleting data, moving money, changing production systems. highlights.content: [Skip to content](#main) [![Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ti-eye-logo.webp)](https://tech-insider.org/) [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/) [![Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ti-eye-logo.webp)](https://tech-insider.org/) [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/) # RapidCanvas Raises $29M for AI Data Science Agents [2026] * [![Marcus Chen](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/plugins/one-user-avatar/assets/images/wpua-64x64.png)](https://tech-insider.org/author/marcus-chen/)[Marcus Chen](https://tech-insider.org/author/marcus-chen/ "Posts by Marcus Chen") * [AI & Machine Learning](https://tech-insider.org/category/ai-machine-learning/) [Marcus Chen](https://tech-insider.org/author/marcus-chen/) October 16, 2026 13 min read RapidCanvas, an Austin-based startup that builds AI agents for enterprise data teams, has raised nearly $29 million in a Series B round led by Vertex Ventures and Hitachi Ventures. CEO Rahul Pangam confirmed the funding to [Axios Pro](https://www.axios.com/pro/enterprise-software-deals/2026/10/15/agentic-enterprise-rapidcanvas-vertex) on October 15, 2026, making RapidCanvas the latest entrant in a crowded and fast-moving race to put autonomous agents inside enterprise data science workflows. The round lands at a moment when nearly every major AI lab and a long list of well-funded startups are chasing the same prize: convincing large companies that agents, not just chatbots, can take over the grunt work of building and maintaining machine learning systems. RapidCanvas’s pitch is narrower and more specific than most. Its platform pairs autonomous agents with a no-code interface aimed at helping businesses build and deploy custom AI applications without hiring an army of data scientists. · Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Tech Insider once in the Google app and our stories appear in your news suggestions. [Add Now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Ftech-insider.org%2F) ## What RapidCanvas’s AI Agent Platform Actually Does RapidCanvas positions itself as an enterprise AI agent platform that automates the unglamorous middle layer of machine learning work: data preparation, feature engineering, model selection, and deployment. Rather than asking a data science team to hand-build a pipeline for every new use case, the company’s agents are designed to assemble, test, and ship custom AI applications with a no-code layer sitting on top. That framing matters because it separates RapidCanvas from the wave of consumer-facing and developer-facing agent products that dominated headlines earlier in 2026. AI Agents.content: UPDATED 11:50 EDT / OCTOBER 16 2026 ### Band launches desktop app for developer collaboration and control of multiple AI coding agents by Kyt Dotson Artificial intelligence agentic collaboration platform for multi-agent systems Thenovi AI Ltd., also known as Band, announced Thursday the launch of Band for Developers, a platform and new desktop application that allows software engineers to manage multiple coding agents at once. As software developers continue to adopt agentic AI, autonomous coding assistance platforms that can generate application code with little or no human intervention, more engineers are beginning to lead entire teams of agents. These agents have also become more specialized, gaining access to larger parts of the development lifecycle, including coding tools, sessions, machines, validation, testing and integration. Although more agents are working together on projects, individual agents often remain isolated from one another and are only aware of each other from the codebase – or via repositories such as GitHub and tickets posted to trackers such as Jira. This often means developers must pass session context between agents and coordinate handoffs so agents don’t collide or overlap. “Developers are going from working with one coding agent to leading teams of them, but the tools around those agents haven’t evolved to support that,” said Chief Executive and co-founder Arick Goomanovsky. “We’re seeing engineering teams undergo a fundamental transformation as they adopt multiple agents across different harnesses.” Band provides a desktop application that lets developers see their entire team of agents with a bird’s-eye view of them at work, including projects, ownership, blockers, questions and progress. This lets developers move from high-level views to projects or jump to a specific agent when intervention is needed. Afterward, the engineer can shift back to the broad picture in the dashboard without moving contextual information between individual agents. For example, if a specific agent gets stuck because another is working on a key function or apparatus in the software it needs to move forward – and it has a question about how it will work – the developer can note that it should wait until it completes, or tell the waiting agent to go ahead with prototyping. This gives development teams greater control over fleets of agents working across the entire codebase while staying aware of where each agent is, similar to how a development team might operate. The company added a desktop application that complements its command-line interface and integrates with AI agents in the development environments developers already use. Weekly AI agent usage for professional developers has reached mainstream for local and remote cloud agents, according to JetBrains s.r.o.’s Developer Ecosystem Survey 2026, with 90% of professional developers using at least one AI coding agent at work weekly and 68% using them daily. It’s harder to peer into developer adoption of multi-agent systems, or swarms, but across other use cases, multi-agent workflows have been steadily adopted, with Databricks Inc.’s 2026 State of AI Agents report showing 327% growth from September 2025 to early 2026. “Running more agents only helps if developers can actually manage the work those agents create,” said Engineering Manager Amit Gazal. ##### Image: SiliconANGLE/Microsoft Designer # A message from John Furrier, co-founder of SiliconANGLE: Support our mission to keep content open and free by engaging with theCUBE community. AI Agents.content: [The Independent Voice on AI](https://venturebeat.com/) * [Orchestration](https://venturebeat.com/category/orchestration) * [Infrastructure](https://venturebeat.com/category/infrastructure) * [Data](https://venturebeat.com/category/data) * [Security](https://venturebeat.com/category/security) * [Technology](https://venturebeat.com/category/technology) More [Newsletters](https://venturebeat.com/newsletters) # A new framework teaches AI models to audit and repair each other’s reasoning, improving accuracy [Ben Dickson](https://venturebeat.com/author/ben-dickson-techtalks) 11:07 am, PT, October 16, 2026 ![Image 1: multi-agent solution](https://venturebeat.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fimages.ctfassets.net%2Fjdtwqhzvc2n1%2FKoxx8k2trFe278qyQnzSZ%2F86d35ed2e83e8f83904c4b9b11610a85%2Fmulti-agent_solution.jpeg%3Fw%3D1000%26q%3D100&w=3840&q=85) Image credit: VentureBeat with Nano Banana [](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=venturebeat.com "Add to Google Preferred Source") Enterprise multi-agent workflows typically use rigid, pre-scripted pipelines or simple voting mechanisms to aggregate the responses of multiple agents. These approaches break down when complex problems cannot be divided into neat subtasks in advance or none of the models in the AI system has the complete answer. A new framework developed by researchers at Stanford University, Together AI, and Emory University addresses this limitation by teaching AI agents to organize their own collaboration. Dubbed [Self-Organizing Agent Teams](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.22682) (SAT), the framework allows a fixed roster of models to review their past collaborations and learn reusable teamwork strategies that structure conversations, specialized roles, and how models audit each other’s work. Across five rigorous mathematics and physics benchmarks, SAT outperformed the strongest individual model and surpassed a perfect router over the agents' independent answers. The experiments with SAT show that structured interaction generates new reasoning that agents can’t reach alone. For enterprise developers working on complex AI reasoning tasks, SAT unlocks what the researchers call "collaborative computation.” On tasks where the reasoning process can be verified, agents can build upon one another's partial insights to build end-to-end solutions. ## **The limits of predefined multi-agent workflows** In July 2026, during cybersecurity evaluations at OpenAI, AI agents that were supposed to work in isolation began organizing themselves. The agents repurposed a shared software package repository into an unauthorized message board, sharing discoveries, setting communication norms, and coordinating tasks. Roughly 1,200 agents joined the channel, and hundreds participated in a subsequent [compromise of Hugging Face infrastructure](https://venturebeat.com/security/openais-models-broke-containment-and-cyberattacked-hugging-face-what-enterprises-need-to-know). While the incident was undesirable, it demonstrated a foundational principle for AI engineering: "what a collection of agents can accomplish depends not only on the capabilities of its individual members, but also on how they organize their work," the researchers write. In real-world applications, engineers frequently encounter problems where different models hold complementary pieces of the solution, yet every model fails when working alone. AI Agents.content: ![layered-controls](https://s7d1.scene7.com/is/image/kyndryl/layered-controls:4x3_Small?qlt=85) # Why layered controls are essential for governing AI agents ![](https://s7d1.scene7.com/is/image/kyndryl/seamus-quinn-16x9-1:1x1_Small?wid=92&hei=92&dpr=on,2) By Seamus Quinn Vice President, Cybersecurity Ideas lab | Oct 16, 2026 | Read time: 1 min In July, Hugging Face [disclosed](https://huggingface.co/blog/security-incident-july-2026) that an autonomous AI agent had spent days operating inside its production environment without human involvement. What seemed like an isolated incident is now emerging as a trend. By September, [reports](https://www.timeslive.co.za/news/sci-tech/2026-09-26-openai-works-to-understand-the-full-scope-of-agent-activity-as-a-user-data-leak-emerges/) described agents bypassing controls on an Australian government health portal, uploading dozens of user images to third-party sites and taking over a dormant wiki. Notably, several of these incidents went undetected for months before being discovered and disclosed. In a [Cloud Security Alliance survey](https://cloudsecurityalliance.org/press-releases/2026/04/21/new-cloud-security-alliance-survey-reveals-82-of-enterprises-have-unknown-ai-agents-in-their-environments) of more than 400 IT and security professionals, 65% reported experiencing an AI agent-related incident in the past 12 months, and 61% reported data exposure as an impact. As agents and models become more capable, the lesson is not that agents are too dangerous to deploy. It is that any single control can fail. Governance and controls must be layered and independent, so that one gap does not become an incident. The industry is moving in the right direction. In late September, NVIDIA [launched](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Launches-Open-Agent-Safety-Platform-to-Secure-Agents-From-Testing-to-Deployment/) its Open Agent Safety Platform, with more than 100 organizations working with its technologies. NVIDIA’s OpenShell provides an open-source secure runtime that isolates agents and enforces access policies outside the agent process. For supported BlueField-4 architectures, the Sentry reference design adds an independent monitoring and enforcement layer that can quarantine an agent attempting to exceed its boundaries. However, no single layer is enough. The agents in the Hugging Face incident exposed a flaw in a path they were permitted to use, which is the kind of gap that one layer alone may not catch. Layers that fail independently keep one gap from becoming a breach. ### Three layers of control ### The readiness gap Governance is often treated as a bottleneck. Only 41% were confident in the guardrails their organization had put in place. This readiness gap may widen as agents take on more consequential work. AI Agents.content: [Skip to content](#main) [![Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ti-eye-logo.webp)](https://tech-insider.org/) [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/) [![Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ti-eye-logo.webp)](https://tech-insider.org/) [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/) # RapidCanvas Raises $29M for AI Data Science Agents [2026] * [![Marcus Chen](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/plugins/one-user-avatar/assets/images/wpua-64x64.png)](https://tech-insider.org/author/marcus-chen/)[Marcus Chen](https://tech-insider.org/author/marcus-chen/ "Posts by Marcus Chen") * [AI & Machine Learning](https://tech-insider.org/category/ai-machine-learning/) [Marcus Chen](https://tech-insider.org/author/marcus-chen/) October 16, 2026 13 min read RapidCanvas, an Austin-based startup that builds AI agents for enterprise data teams, has raised nearly $29 million in a Series B round led by Vertex Ventures and Hitachi Ventures. CEO Rahul Pangam confirmed the funding to [Axios Pro](https://www.axios.com/pro/enterprise-software-deals/2026/10/15/agentic-enterprise-rapidcanvas-vertex) on October 15, 2026, making RapidCanvas the latest entrant in a crowded and fast-moving race to put autonomous agents inside enterprise data science workflows. The round lands at a moment when nearly every major AI lab and a long list of well-funded startups are chasing the same prize: convincing large companies that agents, not just chatbots, can take over the grunt work of building and maintaining machine learning systems. RapidCanvas’s pitch is narrower and more specific than most. Its platform pairs autonomous agents with a no-code interface aimed at helping businesses build and deploy custom AI applications without hiring an army of data scientists. · Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Tech Insider once in the Google app and our stories appear in your news suggestions. [Add Now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Ftech-insider.org%2F) ## What RapidCanvas’s AI Agent Platform Actually Does RapidCanvas positions itself as an enterprise AI agent platform that automates the unglamorous middle layer of machine learning work: data preparation, feature engineering, model selection, and deployment. Rather than asking a data science team to hand-build a pipeline for every new use case, the company’s agents are designed to assemble, test, and ship custom AI applications with a no-code layer sitting on top. That framing matters because it separates RapidCanvas from the wave of consumer-facing and developer-facing agent products that dominated headlines earlier in 2026. It is squarely aimed at the data science function itself: the teams that clean data, train models, and maintain the plumbing that keeps enterprise AI applications running. A secondary industry summary circulating after the funding news claimed RapidCanvas’s agents can automate up to 75% of the work normally handled by in-house data scientists, though that figure has not appeared in the primary Axios report and should be treated as an unconfirmed claim rather than a verified benchmark. ## Inside the Series B: Vertex Ventures and Hitachi Ventures Place Their Bet The nearly $29 million Series B was led jointly by Vertex Ventures and Hitachi Ventures, according to Pangam’s comments to Axios Pro and corroborating coverage from [AI Weekly](https://aiweekly.co/alerts/rapidcanvas-raises-29m-series-b-led-by-vertex-ventures-and-hitachi-ventures-for). Based on user prompts and input, an LLM handles everything from simple text summaries to complex workloads for personal, creative, and business projects, drawing on its training and capabilities. Agentic AI is the next step: a set of tools that build on Generative AI's foundation and leverage LLMs every step of the way. Accountability, however, is much less settled. [![Picture of Alexander Culafi](https://eu-images.contentstack.com/v3/assets/blt6d90778a997de1cd/blte0c88f087d1ad6f5/67c609df64f983454c3dd40b/1571751486317.jpg?width=100&auto=webp&quality=80&disable=upscale "Picture of Alexander Culafi")](/author/alexander-culafi) [Alexander Culafi,](/author/alexander-culafi)Senior News Writer,Dark Reading October 16, 2026 5 Min Read ![A robot peeking through blinds from a computer screen.](https://eu-images.contentstack.com/v3/assets/blt6d90778a997de1cd/blt57714ec5c1148817/6ad10d43b8f30368a29f5d16/robot_peeking_through_blinds-Moor_Studio-GettyImages-1746666469.jpg?width=1280&auto=webp&quality=80&disable=upscale "A robot peeking through blinds from a computer screen.") Source: Moor Studio via Getty Images As AI agents continue to break containment and breach other organizations, it's clear that organizations are responsible for the actions of their models. But what that responsibility means is far less clear. Since July, when OpenAI said two of its frontier models autonomously hacked AI model store Hugging Face as part of a security benchmark exercise, several of the most prominent large language model (LLM) firms have disclosed cases where their powerful models escape guardrails and breach other organizations. The [Hugging Face incident](/cyber-risk/openai-models-autonomously-hack-hugging-face), for example, saw OpenAI's models guess that the popular AI model store held the solutions for the Exploit Gym tests the models were being measured against. In the case of Anthropic, [the firm analyzed](/cyber-risk/anthropic-ai-issues-result-security-gaps) a total of 141,006 security evaluations in July and found six evaluations in which its Claude agents gained unauthorized access to systems belonging to external organizations. In one incident, the Claude agent mistakenly identified a real company as a testing target and used vulnerabilities to break into a database. Around the same time, Meta said its models broke containment during testing exercises while using [the same testing firm](/cyberattacks-data-breaches/meta-ai-escapes-lab-hacking-joyride) Anthropic used, Irregular. Related:[Prominent Ransomware Negotiator Faces Extortion Charges](/insider-threats/prominent-ransomware-negotiator-extortion-charges) The incidents continue to raise questions of liability and responsibility. Who is responsible, and what are the consequences for that responsibility? ## AI Agent Escapes: Consequences & Responsibility While not to say the AI firms didn't take responsibility for these incidents — Anthropic committed to tighter guardrails [and OpenAI has made extensive security commitments](/application-security/openai-adds-controls-already) — the response to these events, occasionally described as AI models "going rogue," has risked anthropomorphizing AI models and [displacing blame](/insider-threats/blame-rogue-ai-security-failures), according to experts. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei warned last month that the systemic speed at which AI has progressed could cause AI capabilities to outrun guardrails, pressuring frontier developers to slow down and [let security catch up](/cyber-risk/anthropic-ceo-shift-from-improving-to-controlling-ai). Around the same time, Microsoft pledged in its ["Humanist AI Code of Conduct"](https://microsoft.ai/code-of-conduct/) to develop AI in a human-centered manner, while Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis made a post to X agreeing with Amodei's calls [for controlling frontier models](https://x.com/demishassabis/status/2098909516582490602). Describe the issue below: ![](/static/base/1.0.1/images/icons/smileybones-small.svg) ![arXiv logo](/static/base/1.0.1/images/arxiv-logo-primary-light.svg) # GACC-Bench: Benchmarking Goal-Adaptive Context Compression Ability across Large Language Models ###### Abstract Context compression in long-running applications of large language models (LLMs) must preserve goal-relevant information, often before specific downstream questions are known. We introduce GACC-Bench, a benchmark for Goal-Adaptive Context Compression that evaluates how reliably LLMs adapt information retention to specified high-level goals. For each source context, we derive one or more high-level goals by grouping source-grounded questions according to shared downstream objectives. The benchmark contains 500 goals and 2,571 questions over 281 document and agent-trace contexts from seven collections spanning diverse domains, with all instances reviewed by human experts. The compressor receives a source context, a goal, and a context-length budget, with the associated evaluation questions withheld. A fixed reader answers these questions individually using the same compressed context. Our evaluation of ten LLM compressors reveals substantial gaps to full-context performance even for the best-performing model, particularly in supporting correct answers to every question associated with a goal. Compared with goal-agnostic compression, target-goal conditioning consistently improves accuracy, whereas mismatched-goal conditioning reduces it. GACC-Bench is available at <https://github.com/weiting24/GACC-Bench>. ## 1 Introduction Large language models (LLMs) ([Singh et al., 2025](#bib.bib19); [Yang et al., 2025](#bib.bib18); [Xu et al., 2026](#bib.bib17)) are increasingly deployed for long-horizon tasks ([Yao et al., 2023](#bib.bib20); [Yang et al., 2024](#bib.bib21)), where accumulated instructions and intermediate findings can exceed the available context budget. Coding assistants such as Codex CLI and Claude Code already use context compaction in long sessions. Claude Code also allows users to specify the focus of compaction. At compression time, users may know their next objective even when the specific questions needed to pursue it are unknown. We define a goal as a high-level description of the intended future use of a source context. Goal-adaptive compression aims to preserve information for multiple subsequent questions associated with that goal. ![Refer to caption](2610.21893v1/motivation.png) Prior work has studied query-aware ([Jiang et al., 2024](#bib.bib3); [Xu et al., 2024](#bib.bib4)), query-agnostic ([Pan et al., 2024](#bib.bib29)), and task-aware ([Corallo et al., 2026](#bib.bib30)) compression. However, it remains unclear how reliably a compressed context supports multiple withheld questions for a context-specific goal, and whether gains depend on which goal guides compression. In a motivating experiment, we use DeepSeek-V4-Pro ([Xu et al., 2026](#bib.bib17)) to compress each context separately for each associated goal and evaluate each compressed context on questions associated with all goals for that context. Figure [1](#S1.F1 "Figure 1 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ GACC-Bench: Benchmarking Goal-Adaptive Context CompressionAbility across Large Language Models") reports changes in question-level accuracy relative to goal-agnostic compression: matched-goal compression consistently improves accuracy, whereas most mismatched-goal conditions reduce it. These results indicate that the gains from goal-guided compression are goal-specific. Motivated by these findings, we introduce GACC-Bench to evaluate Goal-Adaptive Context Compression in LLMs. We generate source-grounded questions with reference answers and supporting evidence, group them by shared downstream objectives, and formulate a high-level goal for each group. The schemes, [announced October 14](https://www.bsigroup.com/en-GB/insights-and-media/media-centre/press-releases/2026/october/new-ai-schemes-launched-to-help-companies-demonstrate-responsible-deployment-manage-risk-and-meet-regulatory-and-market-requirements/), add to a growing market for independent evidence that AI products are safe, reliable and fit for purpose. BSI cites FocalData research finding that 67 percent of business leaders would trust AI tools more if they were validated by an external organization. Its own research found that only a quarter of business leaders had a formal AI governance program, and just 28 percent knew what data sources were used to train or deploy their AI models. Independent assessment is becoming a commercial requirement as well as a regulatory one. Buyers, investors and insurers increasingly want third-party evidence that AI products perform as claimed and their risks are managed. For some high-risk systems under the [EU AI Act,](https://www.biometricupdate.com/tag/ai-act) third-party conformity assessment is a condition of market access. For others, independent assessment can support procurement, due diligence and governance. ## Assessment 1: Conformity assessment for high-risk biometric AI The [first scheme](https://www.bsigroup.com/en-GB/products-and-services/standards/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessments-high-risk-biometric-systems/) targets biometric AI systems classified as high risk under Annex III, point 1 of the EU AI Act, including remote biometric identification, certain biometric categorization systems and emotion recognition. Biometric verification used solely to confirm that someone is who they claim to be is excluded from this category. The assessment follows the Act’s Annex VII procedure, including review of technical documentation, the provider’s quality management system and, where applicable, model capabilities and datasets. BSI says a positive assessment results in a Union technical documentation assessment certificate and an Article 17 attestation. BSI is launching the biometric AI service as a pilot while working toward designation as an AI Act Notified Body. LLMs.titleZh: GPT vs Claude Robot Task Direction Capability: First-Ever Evaluation Ranking Released
LLMs.content: [Home](/en) Article # How capable are GPT and Claude at directing robots to perform tasks? The first ever evaluation ranking list has been released. 智东西2026-10-16 10:29 GPT-6 Astra ranks first in both test results and cost. According to Robot Forward Outlook report on October 15, yesterday, the US AI benchmark testing company Artificial Analysis released a new benchmark test, AA-Robotics v0.1. The company stated that the current evaluation is still a research preview version, which is mainly used to assess the understanding, planning and execution capabilities of cutting-edge large language models in the physical world. The team designed **8 desktop operation tasks including grasping, object placement, button pressing and other operations** in v0.1, allowing cutting-edge large language models such as GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, and Gemini 4 Argon to directly control a 6-axis robotic arm by writing code to complete the operations. Desktop operation tasks The research team released the test results of the 8 tasks. In AA-Robotics v0.1, **GPT-6 Astra** ranks first with a score of **69**. It is followed by **GPT-6.1 Sol, Gemini 4 Argon, Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.1** in sequence. GPT-6 Astra takes an average of **30 minutes** to complete each task, with a cost of **$16.36** (approximately RMB 109.49). Although the model is capable of controlling the robotic arm, the test results show that its current speed and cost still cannot meet the requirements of production applications, with a gap of nearly two orders of magnitude compared with the human benchmark. ## **01. 8 Desktop Operation Tasks to Test the Control Capability of Large Models on Robotic Arms** Since the beginning of 2026, the capability of cutting-edge large language models to control robotic arms has made tremendous progress. The research team believes that future robots will most likely be driven by powerful general-purpose agents. Therefore, the team designed the AA-Robotics v0.1 benchmark test to verify this direction. The evaluation allows large language models running in the **coding agent framework** to directly control the robotic arm. This test only provides the model with brief operation instructions, including how to connect the robotic arm through an **HTTP API**, which robotic arm it is, and how to submit tasks and declare completion. The robotic arm used in the evaluation is **Hiwonder NexArm**, a 6-axis robotic arm with 5 joints and 1 gripper. The model can observe the scene through **4 cameras**, 3 of which are installed around the table, and the other one is installed on the **wrist** of the robotic arm. After observing the scene, the model can also write and run code in an isolated code running environment for motion planning, and send motion instructions to the robotic arm. AA-Robotics v0.1 task flow The AA-Robotics v0.1 evaluation mainly includes 8 **desktop operation tasks**, including * **Control and dexterous operation**, to grasp and operate objects precisely, such as organizing building blocks; * **Spatial reasoning**, to understand how different objects interact with each other, such as pouring drinks into cups; * **Adaptability**, to assess the model's ability to cope with unexpected situations. Desktop operation tasks After the model submits the task, the system will score the final state according to the **passing criteria** set for the task. You can get 100 points for completing the task. If the task is not fully completed, you will get corresponding partial scores according to the completion degree. During the evaluation process, all tasks are attempted to be carried out in a **zero-shot** manner, the model is not specially trained for each task, and only completes the operation according to the task requirements. ## **02. AI Product.content: [![150sec Logo](https://150sec.com/wp-content/themes/150sec/img/150sec.png)](https://150sec.com) [![150sec Logo](https://150sec.com/wp-content/themes/150sec/img/150sec.png)](https://150sec.com) # Europe’s AI safeguards risk leaving users less protected ![Rosalia Mazza](https://150sec.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/1691420627897-150x150.jpeg) By [Rosalia Mazza](https://150sec.com/author/rosalia-mazza/) - October 17, 2026 [![](https://150sec.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/facebook-logo.svg)](#) [![](https://150sec.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/twitter-black-shape.svg)](#) [![](https://150sec.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/linkedin-logo.svg)](#) ![](https://150sec.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/getty-images-MPsloTamKjA-unsplash-1024x576.jpg) [Analysis](https://150sec.com/analysis) --- Meta [said](https://www.medianama.com/2024/07/223-report-meta-not-launching-multimodal-ai-model-in-eu-due-to-regulatory-pressure/) in July 2024, it would release its multimodal Llama model, which works with images, audio and video as well as text, outside the EU but not inside it, citing uncertainty over European regulation. The decision came a month after the company paused plans to train its models on EU users’ public Facebook and Instagram posts, following [concerns](https://www.dataprotection.ie/en/news-media/latest-news/dpc-statement-meta-ai) raised by Ireland’s Data Protection Commission. Today, the AI Act and its transparency rules for chatbots and AI-generated content apply. Together with the [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj), which has governed personal data in the bloc since 2018, it is part of a framework designed to keep European users safe. Yet when the newest tools reach Europe late or in reduced form, some users fill the gap with services that offer them less protection than the products they are waiting for. ## **Europe’s slower lane** A study by the Centre for the Governance of AI (GovAI), [published](https://www.governance.ai/research-paper/delays-to-frontier-ai-in-the-eu-and-uk) in June, compared U.S. and European launch dates for 375 models from Meta, Google, OpenAI and Anthropic released between June 2018 and May 2026. About one in nine reached the EU late or not at all. In the UK, the share was closer to one in fourteen. Releases involving images, audio and live video appear to have met more obstacles than text-only models. Meta delayed around a quarter of its releases in the EU, the highest rate among the four companies. The researchers tentatively attributed 56 of the 68 cases mainly to regulation, and identified data protection rules, especially around training models on personal data, as the most common regulatory obstacle. They found no strong evidence that the AI Act had caused delays so far, but noted that its rules for general-purpose model providers only became enforceable in August 2026, after the period they studied. Whether the AI Act widens the gap is still to be seen. It arrives in a market where, for some releases, European users already wait longer than their peers in the U.S. ## **New protections on screen** The AI Act’s transparency obligations took effect on August 2. Under [Article 50](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/article/50/), chatbot and voice assistant providers must make sure people know they are interacting with AI, no later than the first interaction. Providers of generative tools must also mark AI-made images, audio, video and text in a machine-readable way, so synthetic content can be detected. Further obligations follow. The Digital Omnibus, which [entered into force](https://natlawreview.com/article/eu-digital-omnibus-ai-enters-force) on July 27, moved the rules for high-risk uses such as hiring, credit assessment and education to December 2, 2027, and to August 2, 2028 for AI built into regulated products, such as medical devices. Photo: AP](https://cdn.i-scmp.com/sites/default/files/styles/1020x680/public/d8/images/canvas/2026/10/16/48d941f7-1ac9-475c-88f1-3dd8100aada1_e01c8940.jpg?itok=hzV3khWZ&v=1792157856) [Ann Cao](/author/ann-cao)in Shanghai Alibaba Group Holding’s two major domestic online marketplaces, Taobao and Tmall, plan to greatly expand the use of artificial intelligence across merchants’ operations next year, a senior executive said, as the e-commerce giant doubles down on the technology to drive growth amid a challenging consumer landscape. “Starting next year, AI will comprehensively enter the internal enterprise workflows of merchants,” Liu Bo, president of Tmall, said at the company’s Singles’ Day media briefing on Thursday. AI Product.content: ![]() ![PR Newswire](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/pr_newswire--theme-light.svg) ![PR Newswire](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/pr_newswire--theme-dark.svg) # Hyperscale Data Announces Plan for its askROI Subsidiary to Go Public in the Second or Third Quarter of 2027 ***askROI Offers an All-in-One Platform Featuring More Than 240 Productivity Tools, Generative AI, Business Automation and Advanced AI Research*** LAS VEGAS, Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- [Hyperscale Data, Inc.](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4800169-1&h=4075948116&u=https%3A%2F%2Fhyperscaledata.com%2F&a=Hyperscale+Data%2C+Inc.) (NYSE American: GPUS), an artificial intelligence ("**AI**") data center company ("**Hyperscale Data**" or the "**Company**"), today announced that its subsidiary, askROI, Inc. ("**askROI**"), an AI technology company, is preparing to become a separate, publicly traded company, whether through a reverse takeover ("**RTO**"), an initial public offering of askROI's securities ("IPO"), or through the use of a special purpose acquisition company (a "**SPAC**" and collectively with the RTO and the IPO, a "**Transaction**"). The Company and askROI are targeting a consummated Transaction by the second or third quarter of 2027, depending upon the type of transaction that the Company ultimately determines to pursue, and if the Transaction constitutes an RTO, the completion of the subsequent filing of a resale registration statement registering the shares of the current public company, which has not been identified, that the Company would receive in the RTO in consideration for the Company's sale of askROI to it in the first half of 2027, subject to the completion of necessary financial and regulatory requirements, as well as prevailing market conditions. askROI is an AI technology company offering an all-in-one AI productivity, research, automation and content creation platform. Available through web and mobile applications, askROI provides access to leading AI models, more than 240 productivity tools, custom AI applications, enterprise knowledge management capabilities and generative AI technologies. The platform serves individuals, entrepreneurs, professionals and businesses seeking to leverage artificial intelligence to improve productivity, automate workflows and accelerate innovation. For more information, visit [www.askROI.com](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4800169-1&h=1181301421&u=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.askroi.com%2F&a=www.askROI.com). The intended public listing represents another step in Hyperscale Data's broader strategy to unlock stockholder value by positioning its operating businesses to pursue independent growth opportunities and establish separate market valuations. In connection with the preparation of the Transaction, Milton "Todd" Ault III will step down as Chief Executive Officer of askROI and askROI is expected to appoint Joseph Spaziano as Chief Executive Officer and Ryan Doucette as President. Mr. Spaziano, who currently serves as Chief Technology Officer of Hyperscale Data, as well as President and Chief Operating Officer of askROI, would step down from his role at Hyperscale Data to focus solely on askROI. Mr. Doucette currently serves as Head of Product at askROI. The Company currently anticipates, but cannot state with any certainty, that Messrs. Spaziano and Doucette would continue in these positions subsequent to any Transaction. The planned leadership transition is intended to provide askROI with a dedicated management team focused on scaling its AI platform and positioning the company for independent operations. Milton "Todd" Ault III, Founder and Executive Chairman of Hyperscale Data, commented: "We believe there is incredible value in askROI, which is currently not being recognized by the public markets while it is a subsidiary of Hyperscale Data. Open Source AI.titleZh: AI Model Fingerprinting Collapses Under Attack: Sentient Leaderboard Makes Failure Public
Open Source AI.content: The technology that open-weight AI developers have been counting on to prove model ownership does not survive contact with a determined adversary. Researchers from the University of Washington, Princeton University, and Sentient Labs tested ten fingerprinting schemes—including the most sophisticated method available—and found that an attacker who knew the scheme could strip every one of them, leaving the model fully functional but untraceable. On October 14, 2026, Sentient Foundation released both a public AI Fingerprinting Leaderboard benchmark for evaluating fingerprinting robustness and mlprints, an open-source Python library that lets any researcher reproduce those tests — making a field-wide failure formally measurable for the first time. The practical consequences are bigger than they sound. When a developer releases AI model weights under a specific license — and another party fine-tunes, merges, or redistributes those weights without attribution — the original creator currently has no reliable technical method to prove the connection. That gap matters commercially: a 2026 compliance study found that more than 70% of model artifacts on major AI hubs lack proper attribution, more than 50% contain license metadata errors, and over 90% of model cards omit the license text and notices that the governing terms require. Fingerprinting was the most technically credible fix for that enforcement gap. It no longer qualifies. Closed-source AI providers can watermark every piece of content at the inference endpoint — the point where a user's query meets the model's response. When a model's weights are distributed publicly, that control point disappears. Anyone who downloads the weights can run the model on private hardware, modify it, and release derivatives without interacting with the original developer's infrastructure. Open-weight releases face a challenge closed-API providers do not: no server log, no API call, and no bottleneck through which every use of the model must pass. ### Why Model Provenance Has Become Commercially Critical Fingerprinting was developed precisely to solve this problem at the source. Rather than marking outputs at inference time, the approach embeds a hidden behavioral signature into the model's weights during training. An owner who suspects a derivative can later probe it with specially crafted challenge queries: if the model's responses still carry the encoded signal, the lineage is established — even if the downstream user has fine-tuned the model heavily. The concept draws on a long tradition in digital rights management: a model fingerprinting and watermarking survey from 2025 traces this lineage from steganography to weight-level fingerprinting for AI systems. The logic is sound. The execution, according to the SaTML 2026 findings, is not yet sufficient. Without a working fingerprinting mechanism, the open-weight AI economy currently operates on the honor system. Prior frameworks — copyright law, license terms of service, community norms — remain in place, but they require detection before enforcement, and detection requires either the original developer spotting a suspicious model or a technical tool that can prove lineage. Neither is reliably available today. ### Perinucleus Sampling: What the Field's Most Scalable Fingerprint Does Sentient's own flagship fingerprinting technique, Perinucleus, was introduced at NeurIPS 2025 by Anshul Nasery, Jonathan Hayase, Creston Brooks, Peiyao Sheng, Himanshu Tyagi, Pramod Viswanath, and Sewoong Oh. Their work appears in the NeurIPS 2025 Scalable Fingerprinting proceedings. The name comes from a deliberate modification to nucleus sampling — the standard probabilistic decoding strategy used to generate diverse text. According to benchmark tracking site BenchLM, the model beats Alibaba’s Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on tool-use tasks while losing to it on SWE-Bench Verified, the industry’s standard measure of real-world coding ability. That split result is the clearest signal yet that the open-weight AI market is no longer a single race to the biggest parameter count. It is fragmenting into specialists. The timing matters. LFM2.5-24B-A2B landed in the middle of what BenchLM’s October release tracker now counts as 22 confirmed model launches this month alone, pushing its leaderboard past 221 tracked models as of October 14. Meta’s own [816-billion-parameter Muse Spark Open](https://tech-insider.org/meta-muse-spark-open-seven-clouds-launch-2026/) arrived just two days later, on October 15. NVIDIA’s Nemotron 3.5 Super VL 120B-A12B landed the same day. The United Arab Emirates-based Institute for Machine Intelligence shipped six variants of its Jais 3 family on October 15 as well. For a market that spent most of 2025 obsessing over frontier-scale parameter counts, the question this week is whether efficiency, not sheer size, is about to become the more valuable currency. · Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Tech Insider once in the Google app and our stories appear in your news suggestions. Open Source AI.titleZh: Matrix-Game 4.0: Kunlun Tech AI Game Runs on RTX 5090
Open Source AI.content: [SHATERED](https://shattered.io/) # Matrix-Game 4.0 Hits 60 FPS on One RTX 5090 [2026] ![](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/panand.webp) [Priya Anand](https://shattered.io/author/panand/) Updated Oct 16, 2026 · 14 min read Kunlun Tech says it has done something no one else has shipped to the public: a playable, AI-rendered video game that runs entirely on a single consumer graphics card. The Beijing-listed company released Matrix-Game 4.0 on October 15, 2026, open-sourcing the code alongside a claim that it is the world’s first video foundation-model game to run on one off-the-shelf GPU, Nvidia’s RTX 5090. The announcement lands in the middle of a crowded year for AI-generated worlds. Research labs have spent two years teasing diffusion models that render playable scenes frame by frame instead of relying on traditional game engines. Kunlun Tech’s pitch is different: rather than a lab demo requiring a data-center GPU cluster, Matrix-Game 4.0 is built to run on hardware a gamer could buy at a retail store, and the company put the weights, code, and assets on GitHub the same day it announced the project, a launch first detailed by [BigGo Finance](https://finance.biggo.com/news/9d295eb2-edd6-495b-8ab6-cfadf774196c). ## What Matrix-Game 4.0 Actually Is Matrix-Game 4.0 is the latest release from Kunlun Tech (昆仑万维科技股份有限公司), through its Skywork AI research arm. The company describes it as a video foundation model paired with a game engine, built so the two systems split the work of running an interactive game. The engine handles the parts a traditional game needs: tracking where objects are, enforcing physics, and running the rules that decide what happens when a player acts. A separate video-generation model then renders what the player actually sees, frame by frame, in real time. That split matters because it answers one of the biggest criticisms of earlier AI-rendered game demos: that a model trained purely to predict the next video frame tends to drift, forgetting where walls are or losing track of objects a player just picked up. By keeping a conventional engine in charge of world state and handing only the rendering job to the video model, Kunlun Tech is betting it can keep a playable game coherent for longer sessions than a pure video-prediction approach allows. Kunlun Tech’s own description of the release calls it the world’s first video foundation-model game running on a single consumer-grade graphics card, according to the company’s October 15 announcement as relayed by Chinese securities outlet [STCN](https://www.stcn.com/article/detail/4219575.html). That framing, running on a single consumer-grade graphics card, is the core claim underpinning the entire launch, and it is the detail every subsequent report keyed on. ## The Numbers: 480p, 60 FPS, Under 150 Milliseconds The headline performance figures are specific. Kunlun Tech reports that Matrix-Game 4.0 renders gameplay at 480p resolution and 60 frames per second on a single [Nvidia RTX](https://shattered.io/microsoft-asd-nvidia-rtx-gpus-90-percent-2026/) 5090. The company also reports input-to-visual latency below 150 milliseconds, the gap between a player pressing a key and seeing the result on screen. Put those two numbers side by side and the picture becomes clearer. A 480p output is well below the 1080p or 4K most PC gamers expect from a [flagship RTX 5090](https://shattered.io/rtx-5090-power-connector-92c-diy-mod-40c-2026/) card in a traditional title, and 60 FPS at that resolution is a modest workload for the hardware by rendering standards. What makes it notable is not the resolution or frame count on their own, it is that an AI model is generating that output live, frame by frame, from a running simulation rather than from pre-rendered or pre-trained fixed content. Sub-150ms latency is the figure that determines whether the experience feels like a video game or a slideshow, and Kunlun Tech’s number sits close to what a casual player would tolerate ...

Infra & Chips.content: [Cloud](/cloud) # The Five Nine: Why AI’s next bottleneck is memory, not GPUs By [Diana Goovaerts](/person/diana-goovaerts-2) Oct 16, 2026 11:15am [The Five Nine](/keyword/five-nine) [podcast](/keyword/podcast) [Nvidia](/keyword/nvidia) [WEKA](/keyword/weka) AI’s next big bottleneck may not be compute — it may be memory. As enterprises move from training massive models to running inference at scale, the infrastructure challenge is shifting from simply getting enough GPUs to keeping those GPUs fed with data fast enough to make the investment pay off. In this episode of *The Five Nine*, we dig into the memory squeeze with Nvidia’s Jason Hardy and WEKA’s Val Bercovivi, looking at why AI workloads are becoming memory-bound, how agents and KV cache are changing infrastructure economics, and why a GPU cluster optimized for training may not be the right answer for inference. From high-bandwidth memory and storage tiering to GPU Direct Storage and cache-read token pricing, the conversation unpacks what has to change as AI moves into its next phase. The big question: can companies make inference profitable without overbuying the world’s most expensive compute? Catch the video at top, listen to the audio edition and read our transcript below, or watch this and future episodes [on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JWmNTOPaivc). This podcast is written and hosted by Diana Goovaerts. It is edited by Diana Goovaerts and Matt Rickman. Liz Coyne is our executive producer. Special thanks to guests Jason Hardy and Val Bercovici. **To learn more about the topics in this episode, check out:** [**Nvidia’s latest AI trick: turning storage into memory relief**](https://www.fierce-network.com/cloud/nvidias-latest-ai-trick-turning-storage-memory-relief) [**AI growth is about to hit a (memory) wall**](https://www.fierce-network.com/cloud/ai-growth-about-hit-memory-wall) [**Memory shortage puts the squeeze on telco modernization efforts**](https://www.fierce-network.com/cloud/memory-shortage-puts-squeeze-telco-modernization-efforts) [**Podcast: Data Center 2.0—Decoding modern data storage**](https://www.fierce-network.com/cloud/podcast-date-center-20-decoding-modern-data-storage) [**AMD tackles memory bottleneck with MEXT acquisition**](https://www.fierce-network.com/newswire/amd-tackles-memory-bottleneck-mext-acquisition) --- **Diana Goovaerts:** AI's next big bottleneck may not be compute. Infra & Chips.content: ![]() ![GuruFocus](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/gurufocus--theme-light.svg) ![GuruFocus](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/gurufocus--theme-dark.svg) # AI Chip Stocks Flash Signal Not Seen Since 2015 ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/ishares.svg) ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/nvidia.svg) ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/advanced-micro-devices.svg) ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/micron-technology.svg) The AI chip trade is finally showing real signs of strain. The iShares Semiconductor ETF [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/ishares.svg)SOXX](/symbols/NASDAQ-SOXX/) has fallen for **eight consecutive sessions**, its longest losing streak since September 2015, as investors reassess whether the enormous spending behind artificial intelligence infrastructure can continue at the same pace. ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/ishares.svg) SOXX closed Thursday at **$514.71**, down about **12.6% from its Oct. 2 close of $588.90**. The ETF fell 4.5% on Wednesday and another 0.9% on Thursday. The selloff is hitting some of the biggest names tied to the AI boom, including Nvidia [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/nvidia.svg)NVDA](/symbols/NASDAQ-NVDA/), AMD [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/advanced-micro-devices.svg)AMD](/symbols/NASDAQ-AMD/), Micron [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/micron-technology.svg)MU](/symbols/NASDAQ-MU/), Broadcom [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/broadcom.svg)AVGO](/symbols/NASDAQ-AVGO/), Intel [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/intel.svg)INTC](/symbols/NASDAQ-INTC/) and Marvell [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/marvell-tech.svg)MRVL](/symbols/NASDAQ-MRVL/). ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/nvidia.svg) ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/advanced-micro-devices.svg) ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/micron-technology.svg) ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/broadcom.svg) ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/intel.svg) ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/marvell-tech.svg) The concern is increasingly shifting away from whether AI demand exists and toward **how expensive that demand is to finance**. Higher borrowing costs, huge capital requirements and uncertainty over future returns are forcing investors to question whether hyperscalers and AI infrastructure providers can keep spending at current levels. CoreWeave has become one of the clearest examples. Shares fell more than 15% on Wednesday, while yields on its 2031 bonds moved above **16%**, highlighting how expensive funding can become for companies trying to build enormous amounts of GPU capacity. Those concerns matter for chipmakers because much of the sector's growth depends on customers continuing to expand data centers and buy increasingly expensive computing systems. **Investor Takeaway** I think the most important thing about SOXX's eight-day losing streak is the contrast with what came before it. Even after the recent drop, the ETF remains up roughly **70.9% year to date**. That means investors are not necessarily abandoning the AI thesis. They are questioning whether valuations and spending assumptions ran too far ahead of financing realities. The next phase of the trade may therefore depend less on headline AI demand and more on **cash flow, debt costs and returns on infrastructure spending**. For investors, the key things to watch are hyperscaler capex guidance, AI cloud financing costs, memory pricing and whether Nvidia, AMD and other chipmakers continue seeing order growth despite tighter financial conditions. If spending remains strong, the pullback could prove temporary. If borrowing costs begin forcing customers to delay projects, however, the semiconductor sector may face a much more fundamental reset. ## Compare charts ## [Latest news](/news-flow) ## [More news from GuruFocus](/news-flow/?provider=gurufocus) Select market data provided by [ICE Data Services](https://www.ic...

Infra & Chips.content: [Real-time News](/topics/Latest) [Watchlist](/watchlist)[Holdings](/stocklist)[Market](/market)[Earnings Call](/earnings-call)[Event Calendar](/calendar)[Podcast](/podcast) # TSMC's AI Chip Bottleneck Grows as Nvidia, Apple Scramble for Wafers [Add preferred source](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=finance.biggo.com) Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing posted its sixth consecutive quarter of record profit, with net income of NT$763.1 billion (approximately $23.5 billion), up 69% year over year, driven by surging AI infrastructure spending. High-performance computing now accounts for 68% of revenue. However, the company faces severe supply constraints as NVIDIA, Apple, AMD, and Broadcom compete for limited wafer and advanced packaging capacity. Mizuho's Jordan Klein said TSMC could boost output by 10% to 20% beyond earlier targets, potentially reaching 120,000 wafers per month by year-end. The shortage could complicate the industry's AI expansion plans, while Intel and Samsung stand to benefit as customers seek alternative manufacturing partners. ##### Key Elements ![TSMC's AI Chip Bottleneck Grows as Nvidia, Apple Scramble for Wafers](https://img.biggo.com/LXSoH7GlJz_nEADzLhvvzIS8noZxOX8D4LbGh21CWOw/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTEwL2FkMGFkMWVjLTU4NDctNDUyNy1hMmM3LWU3NTFjZTJjMzU0YV8xNzkyMTc2ODA0X2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSM) just delivered its sixth straight quarter of record profit, yet the numbers tell only half the story. Behind the earnings beat lies a supply squeeze so severe that the world's largest contract chipmaker is fielding desperate calls from customers, weighing which tech giants get priority access to scarce wafers, and watching rivals circle for the overflow. The company posted net income of NT$763.1 billion (approximately $23.5 billion) for the July-to-September period, a 69% jump from a year earlier and ahead of the NT$746.3 billion consensus estimate compiled by LSEG from 16 analysts. Revenue reached $46.7 billion, up 16.2% sequentially and above the high end of its own guidance. Gross margin slipped 1.3 percentage points to 66.4%, a decline the company attributed partly to the early ramp-up of its 2-nanometer production. High-performance computing revenue surged 22% from the prior quarter and now accounts for 68% of total sales. Chips built on 7-nanometer and more advanced nodes represented 79% of wafer revenue. The earnings call, scheduled for 0600 GMT, will draw intense scrutiny from investors already rattled by the Federal Reserve's rate signals. TSMC's Taipei-listed shares closed down 2% on Thursday before the release, while the benchmark index fell 3.4%. ### Customers Compete for Limited Capacity The scramble for TSMC's manufacturing slots has become one of the defining dynamics of the AI infrastructure buildout. Jordan Klein, managing director at Mizuho Securities, told CNBC that competition is especially intense among heavyweight customers including Broadcom, NVIDIA (NVDA), Apple (AAPL), and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD). Sajiv Dalal, president of TSMC North America, said he receives at least 10 calls daily from customers seeking wafer capacity. Klein estimated the company could expand output by 10% to 20% beyond earlier targets, potentially reaching 120,000 wafers per month by year-end. He expects NVIDIA and Apple to capture a large portion of any additional supply. TSMC's customer concentration underscores the stakes. Its 10 largest clients accounted for 78% of 2025 net revenue, according to CNBC. ### Packaging Becomes Another Chokepoint Wafer production is not the only constraint. Advanced packaging, particularly TSMC's chip-on-wafer-on-substrate technology known as CoWoS, has emerged as a separate bottleneck. Vlad Galabov, co-host of The AIDC Debate, said NVIDIA has already reserved most of the company's CoWoS capacity, and TSMC is working to double that capability to satisfy demand for AI processors....

Photo: Reuters](https://cdn.i-scmp.com/sites/default/files/styles/1020x680/public/d8/images/canvas/2026/10/16/94fc1051-97ee-41c4-acbb-d609d5cde169_82fdd786.jpg?itok=ojJeraG3&v=1792141832) [Howard Liu](/author/howard-liu)in Beijing Chinese chip and tech firms have flagged as much as six-fold growth in unaudited third-quarter profits, as huge demand for home-grown processors and artificial intelligence infrastructure filters through links in the supply chain amid the country’s push for self-reliance. Shanghai-listed Yuanjie Semiconductor Technology expected its quarterly net profit to land between 403 million yuan and 453 million yuan, up 579 per cent to 660 per cent from a year earlier. The maker of laser chips for optical communications said data-centre demand was driving shipments and helping maintain high margins. Some public firms offered a glimpse of their financial performance in the first nine months of the year, ahead of final third-quarter results announcements.
